content:
The image shows a page from what appears to be a program or biographical compilation in French. It contains biographical entries for two artists:

1. Philippe Minyana - The text describes him as a dramatic author and actor born in 1946 in Besançon, France. After studying literature, he taught from 1971 to 1979. His passion for theater led him to work with directors like Andréi Serban, Benno Besson, and Carlos Wittig. Since 1993, he has been a member of the editorial committee for "Cahiers de Prospero." The text details his extensive theatrical works, collaborations with various directors and theaters, and mentions specific productions including "Jojo" written in 1990.

2. Elena Andreyev - The beginning of her biography appears at the bottom of the page, noting she won first prize for baroque cello at the National Superior Conservatory of Music in Paris under the direction of Christophe Coin. Since 1988, she has been associated with Les Musiciens du Louvre and Les Arts Florissants, and is a member of a string trio.

The page also includes information about someone's regular presence at the Avignon Festival since 1971 and their contributions to musical theater, though this section appears to be about a third person not fully identified in the visible portion.
